title: The hyperbolicity conjecture for semi-symmetric polynomials
statement:
For $n,p\in\mathbb{N}$, define the $p$-homogeneous semi-symmetric polynomial

$$
s_{n,p}(x,\lambda)=\sum_{k=0}^p\frac{\sigma_k(x)\sigma_{p-k}(\lambda)}{\binom{n}{k}},
$$

for $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^p$. Let $\mathbb{I}$ denote the all-ones direction, and call a homogeneous polynomial $\mathbb{I}$-hyperbolic when its restrictions along lines in that direction have only real roots. **Semi-symmetric hyperbolicity conjecture.** The polynomial $s_{n,p}$ is $\mathbb{I}$-hyperbolic. The paper proves that this is equivalent to the corresponding assertion for $s_{p,p}$ and explains that it implies the real-rootedness concavity conjecture; the assertion itself is left open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.10327

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).
source_name: Xavier Lachaume, “On the concavity of a sum of elementary symmetric polynomials”, arXiv:1712.10327 (2017).
